headline: Spanish Usage-First Verbs Foundation
threshold: Sixty verb lemmas in descending Spanish Web 2011 corpus frequency, with new usage scenes. Inflected forms count together; frequency varies by genre and region.

lessons.title: 1. ser · Identifying a new group
lessons.objective: 1. ser · Identifying a new group: Use ser to identify people, describe a group, give origin, and locate an event in time or place.

words.es: Soy el nuevo coordinador del grupo.
words.en: I am the group's new coordinator.

words.es: Somos diez personas de tres ciudades.
words.en: We are ten people from three cities.

words.es: La reunión es en la sala del fondo.
words.en: The meeting is in the room at the back.
Who is the person who is missing?

words.es: Es una compañera que viene de otra oficina.
words.en: It is a coworker who is coming from another office.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing identifying a new group. Use ser to identify people, describe a group, give origin, and locate an event in time or place. It is not interchangeable with estar. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 2. haber · What exists and what is finished
lessons.objective: 2. haber · What exists and what is finished: Use hay for existence.
lessons.focus: 2. haber · What exists and what is finished

words.es: Hay dos carpetas para cada persona.
words.en: There are two folders for each person.
Is there a store near the center?

words.es: Sí, pero ya he comprado una caja.
words.en: Yes, but I have already bought a box.

words.es: Mi compañera ha preparado las mesas.
words.en: My coworker has prepared the tables.

words.es: Todavía no hemos abierto la sala.
words.en: We have not opened the room yet.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing what exists and what is finished. Use hay for existence. Auxiliary haber plus a participle describes completed actions; the participle stays unchanged. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 3. tener · Possession, age and immediate needs
lessons.objective: 3. tener · Possession, age and immediate needs: Tener describes possession and expressions such as tener hambre.
lessons.focus: 3. tener · Possession, age and immediate needs

words.es: Tengo una tarjeta para entrar al edificio.
words.en: I have a card to enter the building.

words.es: Mi compañero tiene la llave de la sala.
words.en: My coworker has the room key.

words.es: Tenemos veinte minutos antes de empezar.
words.en: We have twenty minutes before starting.
Do you have a copy of the list?
No, but I have to print it.

words.es: Los demás tienen tiempo para tomar un café.
words.en: The others have time to have a coffee.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing possession, age and immediate needs. Tener describes possession and expressions such as tener hambre. Tener que + infinitive expresses an obligation; tengo is the irregular yo form. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 4. poder · Ability and permission in a new place
lessons.objective: 4. poder · Ability and permission in a new place: Poder plus infinitive expresses ability, possibility or permission.
lessons.focus: 4. poder · Ability and permission in a new place

words.es: Puedo abrir la puerta con esta tarjeta.
words.en: I can open the door with this card.
Can you help me with the boxes?

words.es: Podemos dejarlas junto a la recepción.
words.en: We can leave them next to reception.

words.es: Hoy no pueden usar el ascensor.
words.en: Today they cannot use the elevator.

words.es: Mi compañera puede mostrar otra entrada.
words.en: My coworker can show another entrance.
Afterward we can start the meeting.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing ability and permission in a new place. Poder plus infinitive expresses ability, possibility or permission. Present puedo changes the stem in stressed forms; podemos keeps o. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 5. estar · Locating people and describing readiness
lessons.objective: 5. estar · Locating people and describing readiness: Use estar for location of people and things and many conditions.
lessons.focus: 5. estar · Locating people and describing readiness

words.es: Estoy junto a la entrada principal.
words.en: I am next to the main entrance.

words.es: Ana está en la segunda sala.
words.en: Ana is in the second room.

words.es: Las cajas están debajo de la mesa.
words.en: The boxes are under the table.
Yes, we are ready to begin.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing locating people and describing readiness. Use estar for location of people and things and many conditions. Events often use ser for their location instead. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 6. hacer · What a group does and makes
lessons.objective: 6. hacer · What a group does and makes: Hacer covers doing and making; learn useful combinations such as hacer una lista and hacer preguntas.
lessons.focus: 6. hacer · What a group does and makes

words.es: Hago una lista de las personas que vienen.
words.en: I make a list of the people who are coming.

words.es: Ana hace las llamadas de confirmación.
Nosotros hacemos una pausa a las diez.
words.en: We take a break at ten.
What are the new coworkers doing?
They ask questions about the schedule.

words.es: Al final hacemos un resumen del plan.
words.en: At the end we make a summary of the plan.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing what a group does and makes. Hacer covers doing and making; learn useful combinations such as hacer una lista and hacer preguntas. Present yo is hago. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 7. decir · Passing on words accurately
lessons.objective: 7. decir · Passing on words accurately: Decir introduces words or information.

words.es: La directora dice que viene en camino.
words.en: The director says she is on her way.

words.es: Yo digo a mis compañeros que esperen aquí.
words.en: I tell my coworkers to wait here.

words.es: ¿Qué dice el mensaje sobre la entrada?
words.en: What does the message say about the entrance?

words.es: Dice que debemos usar la puerta lateral.
words.en: It says we should use the side door.

words.es: No decimos que la reunión esté cancelada.
words.en: We are not saying the meeting is canceled.

words.es: Solo decimos que empezará un poco más tarde.
words.en: We are only saying that it will start a little later.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing passing on words accurately. Decir introduces words or information. Present digo and dices contrast with preterite dije and participle dicho. Decirle algo a alguien means tell someone something. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 8. ir · Destinations and next actions
lessons.objective: 8. ir · Destinations and next actions: Ir uses voy, vas, va, vamos, van.

words.es: Voy a la recepción para preguntar la hora.
words.en: I am going to reception to ask the time.

words.es: Los demás van a preparar el café.
words.en: The others are going to prepare coffee.
Are we going to the large room first?

words.es: No, vamos a esperar junto a la entrada.
words.en: No, we are going to wait next to the entrance.

words.es: Después todos vamos a conocer el edificio.
words.en: Afterward we are all going to get to know the building.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing destinations and next actions. Ir uses voy, vas, va, vamos, van. Ir a + infinitive describes a plan; ir a + place describes a destination. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 9. dar · Giving, thanking and orientation
lessons.objective: 9. dar · Giving, thanking and orientation: Dar commonly gives something to a recipient.

words.es: Doy una carpeta a cada participante.
words.en: I give a folder to each participant.

words.es: La recepcionista nos da un mapa.
words.en: The receptionist gives us a map.

words.es: ¿Me das el número de la sala?
words.en: Will you give me the room number?

words.es: Damos las gracias por la ayuda.
words.en: We thank them for the help.

words.es: Las dos puertas dan al mismo pasillo.
words.en: The two doors open onto the same corridor.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing giving, thanking and orientation. Dar commonly gives something to a recipient. Learn phrases such as dar las gracias and dar a for a window facing somewhere. Present yo is doy. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 10. deber · Recommendations and obligations
lessons.objective: 10. deber · Recommendations and obligations: Deber + infinitive commonly expresses duty or advice.

words.es: Debemos empezar antes de las nueve.
Cada persona debe revisar su nombre.
words.en: Each person should check their name.
Should I also sign the second sheet?

words.es: No, pero deberías guardar una copia.
words.en: No, but you should keep a copy.

words.es: No deben entrar por la puerta cerrada.
words.en: They should not enter through the closed door.

words.es: Podemos pedir ayuda si tenemos dudas.
words.en: We can ask for help if we have questions.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing recommendations and obligations. Deber + infinitive commonly expresses duty or advice. Debería softens a recommendation; deber dinero instead means owe money. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.
